title: Cacio e Pepe
description: Roman pasta with just Pecorino, black pepper and starchy pasta water, tossed into a creamy, peppery sauce in minutes.
scaleNote: Cacio e pepe is easiest in small batches. For 4, use a bigger skillet and toss in two batches if the sauce won’t come together.

image.alt: A plate of spaghetti with pecorino and cracked black pepper

ingredients.scaleNote: A smaller pot of water concentrates the starch that makes the sauce.
Pecorino is salty, so the water is only lightly salted.

steps.text: Bring the water and salt to a boil in the pot and cook the pasta until just shy of al dente. Save {qty 1 1/2 cup fixed} of the pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile toast the cracked pepper in the dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, {time 1 min}. Add {qty 1/2 cup fixed} of pasta water and the butter and let it bubble.
Put the cheese in a bowl and whisk in a few tablespoons of warm (not boiling) pasta water to make a smooth, thick paste.

Add the pasta to the skillet and toss for {time 1 min} over medium heat. Take the pan off the heat, wait {time 30 sec} so it isn’t too hot, then add the cheese paste and toss vigorously, adding splashes of pasta water until glossy and creamy. Serve right away.

notes: If the cheese clumps, the pan was too hot. Add a splash of cool water and keep tossing off the heat.
Grate the cheese on the finest holes of a grater or use a food processor so it melts smoothly.
